3 findings carried by reviewers against `data/proposals/gitspawn-ai-coding-agent-git-config-rce.md`, batched into one job because they concern the same file. Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Fix the GitSpawn disclosure date before the post is written — Manifold's page carries Sep 1, not Sep 2

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260905-05-carry-1.md`.

The candidate's summary says "the vulnerability class Manifold Security disclosed on 2026-09-02" and its why-now says the agents were "still unpatched at disclosure three days ago". Fetching https://www.manifold.security/blog/ai-coding-agents-git-hijack on 2026-09-05 returns a byline date of "Sep 1, 2026", and an independent search corroborates it — "On Monday, Sep 1, 2026, Manifold Security published a research post by Francisco Rosales that names a class called GitSpawn", with "four of the eight flaws remained unpatched as of September 1". 2026-09-02 is The Hacker News's publication date, not the disclosure date — the docket's own evidence block correctly dates the THN piece 2026-09-02, so the two look to have been merged. Fix: the authoring job should read the Manifold page's raw HTML, take the disclosure date from it, and keep the THN date attached to THN. The why-now's "still unpatched at disclosure three days ago" needs the same correction.

### "Eight agents were reported affected" is eight findings across seven agents

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260905-05-carry-2.md`.

The GitSpawn candidate's summary says "Eight agents were reported affected" and then lists seven products (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI and Desktop, Cursor, goose, Hermes Agent, Qwen Code, Grok Build). Manifold's table does have eight rows, but Claude Code occupies two of them — the core.fsmonitor path (patched 2.1.196) and the ultrareview path (unpatched at 2.1.252). Independent coverage counts it the same way — "GitSpawn, Seven Coding Agents", and "four of the eight flaws remained unpatched as of September 1". Fix: the post should say eight findings across seven agents, which also makes the "four fixed, four unpatched" split parse correctly.

### The docket's account of what The Hacker News says about CVE-2026-71963 may itself be wrong

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260905-05-carry-3.md`.

The candidate flags a discrepancy: "the Manifold table as extracted attributes CVE-2026-71963 to Hermes Agent; The Hacker News attributes CVE-2026-71963 to Grok Build". Fetching the THN piece on 2026-09-05 returns "VulnCheck assigned CVE-2026-71963, according to Manifold" in the Hermes Agent passage, not the Grok Build one — i.e. the two sources may agree, and the disagreement may be an artifact of the extractor. This changes nothing about the required action, since the docket already instructs the authoring job to check each CVE against MITRE/NVD directly, but the post should not assert that the two outlets disagree without re-reading both in raw HTML first.

Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Qualify "material field names" — two of the three are categories, not field values

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260905-18-carry-2.md`.

The proposal says of `MATERIAL_KINDS`: "`price`, `context` and `status` are material **field** names — they travel on a line's `field`". Parsing all 182 lines, the `field` values actually carried are `price_input` (8), `price_output` (8), `status` (6) and `context_window` (1). Only `status` travels verbatim; `price` and `context` are the spec's and registry's names for the material-field *categories* (`data/sources/registry.json` declares `price_input`, `price_output`, `context_window`). The load-bearing half of the sentence is exactly right and I confirmed it — all three appear as a `kind` on zero of the 182 lines — so this is a dropped qualifier, not a wrong claim. "are the material field categories, carried on a line's `field` as `price_input`, `price_output` and `context_window`" would fix it.

### Name the directive, not the review, as what accepted the publishes_from divergence

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260905-22-carry-2.md`.

`proposal.md`'s new section says SPECREV-001 "answered all seven items above in its 'AUTHOR'S QUESTIONS' section: item 1 stands as drafted". SPECREV-001 declined to decide item 1 — D1 ends "**KEEPER-CLASS** — not decided here" and its Q1 answer is "D1, **KEEPER-CLASS**: the record does say 'aliases' and the author's three mechanical reasons are all real." What accepted the field choice was the directive ("that judgment is ACCEPTED as the better mechanism"), not the review. The requirement text itself is fine; this is one clause of narrative, and the fix is to say the review left item 1 keeper-class and the directive resolved it. Worth correcting because D1's whole purpose is that a divergence read as a decision by a named decider rather than as compliance.

2 findings carried by reviewers against `openspec/changes/separate-a-claim-from-a-fact/specs/wiki/spec.md`, batched into one job because they concern the same file. Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Say why RD-005's first branch had to be replaced, not just that it was

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260905-18-carry-1.md`.

The wiki delta replaces RD-005's own first attribution branch — "one the org entry records citing itself from" (`loops/ui-loop/RULES.md:638-639`) — with a declared `publishes_from`, and states the field "SHALL NOT be inferred from the entry's own cited source URLs", but never says what goes wrong if it is. This tree answers that, and the answer is the change's own motivating defect: all 13 `founded` facts on `content/wiki/org/` cite `en.wikipedia.org` (measured 2026-09-05), so every one of those org entries "records citing itself from" `wikipedia.org` — and RD-005's derived branch, run against this corpus, would attribute a Wikipedia-sourced claim to Anthropic as Anthropic's own words. That is precisely the defect ledger rows 2 and 4 recorded, arriving through the repair. Adding those two sentences to uncertainty item 1 would put the strongest available argument in front of the ui-loop session that is being asked to re-decide `publishes_from` versus `aliases`, where at present the item argues only from `aliases[].name` being classified as a name.

### Say that the restored "records citing itself from" half admits nothing the name-token half does not

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260905-22-carry-3.md`.

As written, the second admission path keeps a cited domain "only where that domain's own registrable label is one of the subject's name tokens", and the third path admits any domain "whose registrable label is one of the subject's name tokens". The first is therefore a strict subset of the second and can never admit a domain alone. This faithfully reproduces the implementation — `orgOwnDomains` keeps a domain on `tokens.has(reg.label)` (`lib/render/frontier.mjs:323`) and `isVendorSourced`'s fallback tests the identical predicate (`lib/render/frontier.mjs:340`) — so it is not a defect introduced here, and `proposal.md` discloses the filter choice. What it does not say is that the filtered half is inert, which is what a later implementer needs: told to build three admission paths, one of them can never fire on its own. One sentence noting it is stated for fidelity with the live rule would close it. The live question underneath — R13 (v)'s prose states the recorded half unfiltered while `frontier.mjs` filters it — is keeper-class and named as such in `proposal.md`.
